2610.06615.title: COMPASS 2.0: psychometric representational similarity analysis distinguishes symptom structure from personal signal
2610.06615.paper_summary: Language models can score psychiatric questionnaires from speech, but agreement with self-report may reflect the questionnaire rather than the person. We introduce psychometric representational similarity analysis, a framework for comparing the structure of speech-derived scores, self-report, item wording and theory, and implement it alongside person-level construct scoring in COMPASS 2.0. We show how similarly worded items induce covariance without psychological signal. In pre-registered discovery and confirmation analyses of clinical interviews from 275 participants, language-derived symptom geometry resembled wording more than self-report, with no structure beyond wording detected by the registered tests. Geometric agreement with self-report survived assigning participants someone else's answers, whereas person-paired scores captured distress more than specific symptoms. Complementary analyses examined counselling quality and wording structure across 34 instruments and the Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) framework. These findings distinguish agreement about psychological structure from evidence that language-derived assessments track individual people.
2610.06615.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型可以根據語音評分精神病學問卷，但與自我報告的一致性可能反映的是問卷而不是個人。我們引入了心理測量表徵相似性分析，這是一個比較語音衍生分數、 自我報告、項目措辭和理論結構的框架，並在COMPASS 2.0中實施了個人層級的構念評分。我們展示了措辭相似的項目如何在沒有心理信號的情況下引發協方差。在對275名參與者的臨床訪談進行的預註冊發現和確認分析中，語言衍生的症狀幾何形狀更像措辭而非自我報告，註冊測試未檢測到超出措辭的結構。與自我報告的幾何一致性在將參與者的答案分配給他人後仍然存在，而人對人配對的分數捕捉到的痛苦超過了具體症狀。補充分析檢查了34種工具中的輔導質量和措辭結構，以及研究領域標準（RDoC）框架。這些發現區分了對心理結構的一致性和語言衍生評估追蹤個體的證據。
2610.06615.author: Baihan Lin et.al.
